clue.text: Drop item put out in readiness

indicators.note: out, as in 'put out' or disordered, says the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone drops an item and sets it out so it is ready for use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as a phrase about setting things down, but 'put' is part of the anagram fodder and 'out' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe promptness, being quick and prepared to act at once.

clue.text: Dance is almost pathetic after drink

indicators.note: after places the shortened word for pathetic behind the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for pathetic is dropped

parts.note: bad, as in a pathetic, poor effort

explanation.surface: A dance is pretty feeble once the dancer has had a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, an example of the general category.

clue.text: Reported missing before noon

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: mourning, as in grieving for and missing someone gone

explanation.surface: Someone was reported missing before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' looks like a police report, but here it means grieving for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours from dawn until midday are the first part of the day, the time before twelve.

clue.text: Tense intensity containing end of nuclear menace

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: containing says the intensity word wraps round the next letter

parts.note: heat, as in the heat or intensity of a battle

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word nuclear

explanation.surface: A tense, intense standoff over a nuclear menace.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace and a danger looming over someone are synonyms for the same peril.

clue.text: Labour over English tax for deodorant?

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the labour word above the rest

parts.note: toil means hard labour
to try is to tax or strain, as in try one's patience

explanation.surface: Political talk of Labour, English taxes, and then a deodorant tossed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' with its capital looks like the political party; it simply means work. The question mark marks deodorant as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: A deodorant is one example of a washing and grooming product, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Pulled round finally in tatters

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word round

parts.note: ragged means torn, in tatters

explanation.surface: Someone pulled round at the end, though left in tatters.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag something is to haul or pull it, so both are past-tense verbs of hauling.

clue.text: Questioning or tearing apart Conservative

indicators.note: tearing apart: the word apart says these letters are pulled to pieces and rebuilt

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Grilling a Conservative politician, or tearing them to shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tearing' is part of the fodder, and 'apart' alone signals the rearrangement of ORTEARING into INTERROGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives describing something that asks or poses questions, like a sharp tone.

clue.text: European Union move set up for exchange

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a move or turn in a game
laid, as in set down or set the table

explanation.surface: The EU sets up a move for some kind of trade exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is an exchange of words between people, the sense of the noun here.

clue.text: Complete and utter lad dancing with a nude

indicators.note: dancing means the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky lad dancing alongside a naked partner is complete and utter nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete and utter' looks like one phrase, but 'utter' belongs to the fodder; 'with' only links the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean absolute or total, as in sheer, unmixed nonsense.

clue.text: One provides handle worker turns with hesitation

indicators.note: turns says the worker word is read backwards

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in a staff member
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A worker turns round with some hesitation to supply a handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' looks like a tool's grip, but it is slang for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives a name or title to something; a handle is slang for one's name.

clue.text: Breakdown out in Iran, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A breakdown in Iran, unfortunately, puts something out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe collapse, destruction or decay of something.

clue.text: Stamp out Ecstasy spread around clubs

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: around says the spreading word goes about the clubs letter

parts.note: radiate, as in spread outwards
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A campaign to stamp out ecstasy being spread around nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests nightclubs, but it is the card suit, C.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp out is to wipe out or eliminate something completely.

clue.text: Cap put on say, turning icy

indicators.note: put on places the cap word after, in an across clue
turning says the for-example abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
a lid is a cap or top

explanation.surface: Putting a cap on, say, as the weather turns icy.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for freezing cold, very chilly.

clue.text: Leave from son in monarchy

indicators.note: in places the son letter inside the monarchy word

parts.note: reign, the monarch's rule

explanation.surface: A son leaves the monarchy and gives up his place.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at an abdication, which is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a job or post formally is to leave it.

clue.text: Tranquilliser is vet's idea getting doctored

indicators.note: doctored means tampered with, so these letters are altered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tranquilliser is the vet's idea, given to a doctored animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctored' fits the veterinary scene but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranquilliser is a drug that calms, the same thing as a calming drug.

clue.text: Poke single lass getting reckless

parts.note: to prod is to poke
I is the Roman numeral one, single
gal is a girl, a lass

explanation.surface: Poking a single lass is reckless behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastefully extravagant, recklessly spendthrift, as in the parable of the son.

clue.text: Blowing, polish up fiddle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to rub is to polish
a sting is a swindle or fiddle

explanation.surface: Blowing on and polishing up a fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests the violin, but it is a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing up and exploding both describe something breaking open suddenly.

clue.text: Hedonist a bit inhibited by 'hedonist's complaint'

indicators.note: inhibited by says the small bit sits inside the complaint

parts.note: gout is the painful joint condition traditionally blamed on rich living
taken as written
a dab is a small bit

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker is a little held back by an indulgent ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: Gout, long linked with port and rich food, is the stereotypical illness of the self-indulgent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure-seeker who flits about socially; both describe a person who seeks fun.

clue.text: Incompetent builder's front more common in Essex?

indicators.note: front takes the first letter of builder's
in an Essex accent the initial H is dropped, so lose that letter

parts.note: humbler, as in lower in rank, more common

explanation.surface: An incompetent builder is more commonly found in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex, a county east of London, is stereotyped as dropping H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a clumsy, inept person, which the adjective used as a noun describes.

clue.text: Pool perhaps by the empty cell

indicators.note: by puts the next letters beside the game word

parts.note: pool, the cue sport, is an example of a game

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of the word the, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A game of pool by an empty prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cell' suggests a prison, but it is a biological reproductive cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell, such as sperm or egg.

clue.text: Assert casting upset gripping performer

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
gripping means the words hold the wanted letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Casting director asserts something gripping about a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'gripping performer' as the definition, but 'gripping' is the hidden-word indicator: the words hold the letters, which 'upset' turns round. The definition is 'performer'.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a female performer on stage or screen.

clue.text: Dell found in wood in glen

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A dell discovered in a wood in a glen.
explanation.definitionFit: A dingle is a deep wooded hollow, much the same as a small valley.

clue.text: Initially tribal object tribe exalts mystically

definitions.text: Initially tribal object tribe exalts mystically

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A sacred object that a tribe reveres with mystical ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as giving it via the five first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a sacred tribal emblem that a tribe venerates.

clue.text: Calm, catching cold in a bit

indicators.note: catching says the calm word holds the next letters

parts.note: still means calm
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Keeping calm while catching a bit of a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace, a small amount.

clue.text: Slow left on fantastic ship

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the left letter above the ship

parts.note: the Argo was the mythical ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: Slow to leave aboard a fantastic ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning play slowly and broadly.

clue.text: Rejected sweetheart can start to get offensive

indicators.note: rejected, as in turned back, says the sweetheart word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lover is a sweetheart
a tin is a can

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of get

explanation.surface: A rejected sweetheart can start to get nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something disgusting or repellent.

clue.text: Never rained off and on? Strange!

indicators.note: off and on means take every other letter, skipping one then using one

explanation.surface: It never rained, then it rained off and on: how odd!
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean weird or uncanny, unsettlingly odd.

clue.text: Forward motion as prisoners go free

indicators.note: free, as in set loose, says the letters are released into a new order

explanation.surface: Progress in justice reform as prisoners walk free.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving onward step by step is forward motion, advancement.
